¹⁶ A gracious woman earns respect, and strong men hold on to their wealth. ¹⁷ A kind person does good to themselves, but a cruel one brings harm to their own body. ¹⁸ The wicked earn deceitful wages, but those who sow righteousness reap a sure reward. ¹⁹ Righteousness leads to life, but chasing evil leads straight to death. ²⁰ The LORD detests those with a twisted heart, but delights in those who live with integrity.

²¹ Even if the wicked join forces, they will not escape punishment — but the children of the righteous will be delivered. ²² Like a gold ring in a pig's snout is a beautiful woman who has no sense. ²³ The righteous desire only what is good, but what the wicked hope for brings wrath. ²⁴ Some give freely and grow all the richer; others hold back what they should give and end up in poverty. ²⁵ A generous person will prosper, and whoever refreshes others will themselves be refreshed.

²⁶ People curse the one who hoards grain, but they bless the one who sells it. ²⁷ Whoever earnestly seeks good finds favor, but those who pursue evil will find it comes to them. ²⁸ Whoever trusts in riches will fall, but the righteous will flourish like new leaves. ²⁹ Whoever brings trouble on their household will inherit the wind, and a fool will end up serving the wise. ³⁰ The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and whoever wins souls is wise.
³¹ If even the righteous receive what they deserve here on earth, how much more the wicked and the sinful!

¹ Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but whoever hates correction is a fool. ² A good person earns the LORD's favor, but the LORD condemns those who scheme evil. ³ No one can be made secure by wickedness, but the roots of the righteous cannot be shaken. ⁴ A capable wife is a crown to her husband, but one who acts shamefully is like rot in his bones. ⁵ The plans of the righteous are just, but the advice of the wicked is deceitful.

⁶ The words of the wicked lie in ambush for blood, but the mouth of the upright rescues them. ⁷ The wicked are overthrown and are gone, but the house of the righteous stands firm. ⁸ A person is praised according to their wisdom, but those with a twisted heart are despised. ⁹ Better to be a nobody with a servant than to put on airs but have no food. ¹⁰ A righteous person cares for the life of their animal, but even the kindness of the wicked is cruel.

¹¹ Whoever works the land will have plenty of food, but whoever chases fantasies has no sense. ¹² The wicked desire the plunder of evildoers, but the root of the righteous produces fruit. ¹³ The wicked are trapped by their own words, but the righteous escape from trouble. ¹⁴ A person is satisfied with good things through the fruit of their mouth, and the work of their hands comes back to them. ¹⁵ The way of the fool is right in their own eyes, but whoever listens to advice is wise.

¹⁶ A fool's anger is known at once, but a prudent person overlooks an insult. ¹⁷ An honest witness tells the truth, but a false witness tells lies. ¹⁸ Reckless words pierce like a sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing. ¹⁹ Truthful lips endure forever, but a lying tongue lasts only a moment. ²⁰ Deceit fills the hearts of those who plot evil, but those who promote peace have joy.

²¹ No harm comes to the righteous, but the wicked are filled with trouble. ²² The LORD detests lying lips, but those who deal faithfully are his delight. ²³ A prudent person keeps their knowledge to themselves, but fools blurt out foolishness. ²⁴ Diligent hands will rule, but laziness ends in forced labor. ²⁵ Worry weighs down the heart, but a kind word lifts it up.

²⁶ The righteous person is a guide to their neighbor, but the path of the wicked leads them astray. ²⁷ A lazy man doesn't cook what he caught in the hunt, but the diligent person makes use of everything. ²⁸ In the path of righteousness is life, and on that road there is no death.

¹ A wise son accepts his father's discipline, but a mocker refuses correction. ² A person eats well from the fruit of their words, but the treacherous feed on violence. ³ Whoever guards their mouth preserves their life, but whoever talks too freely brings on their own ruin. ⁴ The lazy person craves things and gets nothing, but the diligent is fully satisfied. ⁵ The righteous hate dishonesty, but the wicked bring shame on themselves.

⁶ Righteousness guards the person of integrity, but wickedness brings down the sinner. ⁷ One person pretends to be rich yet has nothing; another pretends to be poor yet has great wealth. ⁸ A person's wealth can ransom their life, but the poor hear no threats. ⁹ The light of the righteous shines brightly, but the lamp of the wicked is snuffed out. ¹⁰ Where there is strife, there is pride, but wisdom is found in those who take advice.

¹¹ Wealth gained dishonestly dwindles away, but whoever gathers it little by little makes it grow. ¹² Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but a dream fulfilled is a tree of life. ¹³ Whoever despises instruction will pay for it, but whoever respects a command will be rewarded. ¹⁴ The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life, turning a person from the snares of death. ¹⁵ Good judgment wins favor, but the way of the treacherous is hard.

¹⁶ Every prudent person acts with knowledge, but a fool exposes their foolishness. ¹⁷ A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a trustworthy envoy brings healing. ¹⁸ Poverty and disgrace come to whoever ignores discipline, but the one who accepts correction is honored. ¹⁹ A longing fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but fools hate to turn away from evil. ²⁰ Walk with the wise and you will become wise, but a companion of fools suffers harm.

²¹ Trouble pursues the sinner, but the righteous are rewarded with good. ²² A good person leaves an inheritance for their children's children, but a sinner's wealth is stored up for the righteous. ²³ There is abundant food in the poor person's field, but it is swept away through injustice. ²⁴ Whoever spares the rod hates their child, but whoever loves them is careful to discipline them. ²⁵ The righteous eat to their heart's content, but the stomach of the wicked goes hungry.

¹ A wise woman builds her house, but a foolish one tears it down with her own hands. ² Whoever walks in integrity fears the LORD, but whoever takes crooked paths despises him. ³ A fool's mouth is a rod of arrogance, but the lips of the wise protect them. ⁴ Where there are no oxen, the stall is clean — but large harvests come from the strength of the ox. ⁵ An honest witness does not lie, but a false witness pours out lies.

⁶ A mocker seeks wisdom but finds none, but knowledge comes easily to the discerning. ⁷ Stay away from a fool, for you will not learn anything from them. ⁸ The wisdom of the prudent is to understand their way, but the folly of fools is deception. ⁹ Fools mock at making amends for sin, but goodwill is found among the upright. ¹⁰ The heart knows its own bitterness, and no outsider can share in its joy.

¹¹ The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of the upright will flourish. ¹² There is a way that seems right to a person, but in the end it leads to death. ¹³ Even in laughter the heart may ache, and rejoicing may end in grief. ¹⁴ The faithless will have their fill of their own ways, and the good person will be satisfied from their own. ¹⁵ A simple person believes anything, but the prudent weighs every step.

¹⁶ The wise fear the LORD and turn away from evil, but a fool rushes ahead recklessly. ¹⁷ A quick-tempered person acts foolishly, and one who schemes is hated. ¹⁸ The simple inherit folly, but the discerning are crowned with knowledge. ¹⁹ Evildoers will bow before the good, and the wicked will bow at the gates of the righteous. ²⁰ The poor are shunned even by their neighbors, but the rich have many friends.

²¹ Whoever despises their neighbor sins, but happy is whoever shows kindness to the poor. ²² Do not those who plan evil go astray? But love and faithfulness belong to those who plan good. ²³ In all hard work there is profit, but idle talk leads only to poverty. ²⁴ The wealth of the wise is their crown, but the foolishness of fools is their folly. ²⁵ A truthful witness saves lives, but a false witness is a fraud.

²⁶ Whoever fears the LORD has a secure fortress, and their children will have a refuge. ²⁷ The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, turning a person away from the snares of death. ²⁸ A large population is a king's glory, but without subjects a prince is ruined. ²⁹ Whoever is slow to anger has great understanding, but a quick temper exalts folly. ³⁰ A peaceful heart gives life to the body, but envy rots the bones.

³¹ Whoever oppresses the poor insults their Maker, but whoever is kind to the needy honors God. ³² The wicked are brought down by their own wickedness, but even in death the righteous have a refuge. ³³ Wisdom rests in the heart of the discerning, but what is inside a fool is plain for all to see. ³⁴ Righteousness lifts up a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any people. ³⁵ The king's favor comes to a servant who acts wisely, but his anger falls on the one who acts shamefully.

¹ A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger. ² The tongue of the wise makes knowledge appealing, but the mouth of the fool gushes foolishness. ³ The eyes of the LORD are everywhere, keeping watch on the wicked and the good. ⁴ A gentle tongue is a tree of life, but a perverse tongue breaks the spirit. ⁵ A fool rejects their father's discipline, but whoever accepts correction shows good sense.

⁶ The house of the righteous holds great treasure, but the income of the wicked brings trouble. ⁷ The lips of the wise spread knowledge, but the heart of the fool is not in it. ⁸ The LORD detests the sacrifice of the wicked, but the prayer of the upright pleases him. ⁹ The LORD detests the way of the wicked, but he loves the one who pursues righteousness. ¹⁰ Stern discipline awaits anyone who leaves the right path; whoever hates correction will die.

¹¹ Even Death and Destruction are open before the LORD — how much more the hearts of people! ¹² A mocker hates to be corrected and will not consult the wise. ¹³ A joyful heart makes a cheerful face, but a troubled heart breaks the spirit. ¹⁴ The discerning heart seeks knowledge, but the mouth of a fool feeds on foolishness. ¹⁵ For the downtrodden, every day is hard — but a cheerful heart has a continual feast.

¹⁶ Better a little with the fear of the LORD than great wealth with turmoil. ¹⁷ Better a simple meal where there is love than a lavish feast with hatred. ¹⁸ A hot-tempered person stirs up conflict, but whoever is patient calms a quarrel. ¹⁹ The way of the lazy is blocked like a hedge of thorns, but the path of the upright is a clear road. ²⁰ A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish person despises their mother.

²¹ Folly brings joy to those with no sense, but whoever has understanding walks a straight path. ²² Plans fail for lack of counsel, but with many advisors they succeed. ²³ A person finds joy in giving just the right reply — and how good is a timely word! ²⁴ The path of life leads upward for the wise, keeping them from going down to the realm of the dead. ²⁵ The LORD tears down the house of the proud, but he sets the widow's boundary firmly in place.

²⁶ The LORD detests the thoughts of the wicked, but gracious words are pure in his sight. ²⁷ Whoever is greedy for unjust gain brings trouble to their family, but whoever hates bribes will live. ²⁸ The heart of the righteous weighs its answers, but the mouth of the wicked pours out evil. ²⁹ The LORD is far from the wicked, but he hears the prayer of the righteous. ³⁰ Bright eyes cheer the heart, and good news refreshes the bones.

³¹ Whoever heeds life-giving correction dwells among the wise. ³² Whoever disregards discipline despises themselves, but the one who accepts correction gains understanding. ³³ Wisdom's instruction is to fear the LORD, and humility comes before honor.

¹ People may make plans in their hearts, but the answer of the tongue comes from the LORD. ² All a person's ways seem pure to them, but the LORD weighs the motives. ³ Commit your work to the LORD, and your plans will succeed. ⁴ The LORD works everything out for his own purpose — even the wicked for the day of disaster. ⁵ The LORD detests everyone who is arrogant in heart — be sure of this: they will not go unpunished.

⁶ Through love and faithfulness sin is atoned for; through the fear of the LORD evil is avoided. ⁷ When the LORD is pleased with someone's ways, he makes even their enemies live at peace with them. ⁸ Better a little with righteousness than great income with injustice. ⁹ In their heart a person plans their course, but the LORD establishes their steps. ¹⁰ The lips of a king speak as an oracle, and his mouth should not betray justice.

¹¹ Honest scales and balances belong to the LORD; all the weights in the bag are his concern. ¹² Kings detest wrongdoing, for a throne is established by righteousness. ¹³ Kings take pleasure in honest lips; they value the one who speaks what is right. ¹⁴ A king's wrath is like a death sentence, but a wise man will appease it. ¹⁵ When a king's face brightens, it means life; his favor is like a rain cloud in spring.

¹⁶ How much better to get wisdom than gold, to get insight rather than silver! ¹⁷ The highway of the upright avoids evil; those who guard their ways preserve their lives. ¹⁸ Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall. ¹⁹ Better to be humble in spirit with the lowly than to share plunder with the proud. ²⁰ Whoever gives thought to a matter will succeed; happy is whoever trusts in the LORD.

²¹ The wise in heart are called discerning, and gracious speech increases persuasiveness. ²² Prudent insight is a fountain of life to the one who has it, but folly is the discipline of fools. ²³ The heart of the wise makes their speech judicious and adds persuasiveness to their lips. ²⁴ Gracious words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the bones. ²⁵ There is a way that seems right to a person, but in the end it leads to death.

²⁶ A worker's appetite works for them — their hunger drives them on. ²⁷ A scoundrel plots evil, and their speech is like a scorching fire. ²⁸ A perverse person stirs up conflict, and a gossip separates close friends. ²⁹ A violent person entices their neighbor and leads them down a bad path. ³⁰ They wink with their eye as they plot perverse things; they purse their lips to carry out their mischief.

³¹ Gray hair is a crown of glory; it is gained by living a righteous life. ³² Better to be slow to anger than to be a warrior, and better to have self-control than to conquer a city. ³³ The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD.

¹ Better a dry crust eaten in peace than a house full of feasting with strife. ² A shrewd servant will rule over a disgraceful son and will share the inheritance among the brothers. ³ Fire tests gold and silver, but the LORD tests the heart. ⁴ A wicked person listens to deceitful lips; a liar pays attention to a destructive tongue. ⁵ Whoever mocks the poor insults their Maker; those who take delight in another's misfortune will not go unpunished.

⁶ Grandchildren are the crown of the elderly, and the glory of children is their parents. ⁷ Eloquent speech is not fitting for a fool — how much less are lies fitting for a ruler. ⁸ A bribe is like a magic stone in the eyes of the one who gives it; wherever they turn, they prosper. ⁹ Whoever covers an offense seeks love, but whoever harps on a matter separates close friends. ¹⁰ A single rebuke does more for a discerning person than a hundred lashes for a fool.

¹¹ A troublemaker seeks only rebellion, so a cruel messenger will be sent against them. ¹² Better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs than a fool bent on their folly. ¹³ Evil will not leave the house of those who repay good with evil. ¹⁴ Starting a quarrel is like breaching a dam — so stop it before it gets out of hand. ¹⁵ Acquitting the guilty and condemning the innocent — the LORD detests them both.

¹⁶ Why should a fool have money in hand to buy wisdom, when they have no desire for it? ¹⁷ A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for a time of adversity. ¹⁸ A person without sense shakes hands on a deal and goes guarantor for their neighbor. ¹⁹ Whoever loves a quarrel loves sin; those who build a high gate invite destruction. ²⁰ Those with a perverse heart find no good, and those with a deceitful tongue fall into trouble.

²¹ Fathering a fool brings grief; having a foolish child gives no joy. ²² A joyful heart is good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones. ²³ The wicked secretly take a bribe to corrupt the course of justice. ²⁴ The discerning fix their eyes on wisdom, but a fool's eyes wander to the ends of the earth. ²⁵ A foolish son brings grief to his father and bitterness to his mother.

²⁶ It is also wrong to fine the innocent, or to flog honest officials for their integrity. ²⁷ Those who have knowledge use words with restraint; those with understanding are even-tempered. ²⁸ Even a fool is thought wise if they keep silent, and discerning if they hold their tongue.

¹ An unfriendly person pursues selfish ends and quarrels with sound judgment. ² A fool takes no pleasure in understanding, only in airing their own opinions. ³ When wickedness comes, so does contempt, and with shame comes disgrace. ⁴ The words of a person's mouth are deep waters; a fountain of wisdom is a bubbling brook. ⁵ It is not good to show partiality to the wicked and so deprive the innocent of justice.

⁶ The lips of a fool invite conflict, and their mouth invites a beating. ⁷ The mouth of a fool is their ruin, and their lips are a trap for their life. ⁸ The words of a gossip are like choice morsels; they go down into the stomach. ⁹ One who is slack in their work is a sibling to one who destroys. ¹⁰ The name of the LORD is a fortified tower; the righteous run to it and are safe.

¹¹ The wealth of the rich is their fortified city; they imagine it a wall too high to scale. ¹² Before a downfall the heart is haughty, but humility comes before honor. ¹³ To answer before listening — that is folly and shame. ¹⁴ The human spirit can endure sickness, but who can survive a crushed spirit? ¹⁵ The heart of the discerning acquires knowledge, for the ears of the wise seek it out.

¹⁶ A gift opens the way and ushers the giver into the presence of the great. ¹⁷ The first to speak in court seems right, until the other comes and cross-examines. ¹⁸ Casting lots settles disputes and keeps strong opponents apart. ¹⁹ An offended friend is harder to win back than a fortified city; disputes are like the barred gates of a citadel. ²⁰ The mouth of a person satisfies their stomach; the produce of their lips fills them.

²¹ The tongue has the power of life and death, and those who love to talk will eat what it produces. ²² Whoever finds a wife finds a good thing and receives favor from the LORD. ²³ The poor plead for mercy, but the rich answer harshly. ²⁴ A person with many friends may be ruined by them, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.

¹ Better to be poor and walk in integrity than to be perverse in speech and be a fool. ² Desire without knowledge is not good — and how much more will hasty feet miss the way! ³ A person's own foolishness leads them astray, yet their heart rages against the LORD. ⁴ Wealth attracts many friends, but the poor are deserted by their friends. ⁵ A false witness will not go unpunished, and whoever pours out lies will not go free.

⁶ Many curry favor with a ruler, and everyone is the friend of those who give gifts. ⁷ The poor are shunned by all their relatives — how much more do their friends avoid them! They pursue them with pleading, but find nothing. ⁸ Whoever gets wisdom loves life; whoever cherishes understanding will prosper. ⁹ A false witness will not go unpunished, and whoever pours out lies will perish. ¹⁰ It is not fitting for a fool to live in luxury — how much worse for a slave to rule over princes!

¹¹ A person's wisdom gives them patience; it is to their glory to overlook an offense. ¹² A king's rage is like the roar of a lion, but his favor is like dew on the grass. ¹³ A foolish child is a father's ruin, and a quarrelsome wife is like a constant dripping. ¹⁴ Houses and wealth are inherited from parents, but a prudent wife comes from the LORD. ¹⁵ Laziness plunges a person into deep sleep, and the idle go hungry.

¹⁶ Whoever keeps the commandment keeps their life, but whoever despises their ways will die. ¹⁷ Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the LORD, and he will repay them for what they have done. ¹⁸ Discipline your children, for in that there is hope; do not be a willing party to their death. ¹⁹ A hot-tempered person must pay the penalty; rescue them, and you will have to do it again. ²⁰ Listen to counsel and accept instruction, so that you may be wise for the rest of your days.

²¹ Many are the plans in a person's heart, but it is the LORD's purpose that prevails. ²² What a person desires is kindness; it is better to be poor than to be a liar. ²³ The fear of the LORD leads to life; a person rests content, untouched by trouble. ²⁴ A lazy person puts their hand in the dish and won't even lift it back to their mouth. ²⁵ Strike a mocker and the simple will learn wisdom; correct the discerning and they gain knowledge.

²⁶ Whoever robs their father and drives out their mother is a child who brings shame and disgrace. ²⁷ Stop listening, my son, to teaching that leads you away from the words of knowledge. ²⁸ A corrupt witness mocks justice, and the mouth of the wicked swallows up iniquity. ²⁹ Penalties are prepared for mockers, and beatings for the backs of fools.

¹ Wine is a mocker and beer is a brawler; whoever is led astray by them is not wise. ² A king's fury is like the roar of a lion; those who provoke him to anger forfeit their lives. ³ It is to a person's honor to avoid strife, but every fool is quick to quarrel. ⁴ A sluggard does not plow in autumn; at harvest time they look and find nothing. ⁵ The purposes of a person's heart are deep waters, but a person of understanding draws them out.

⁶ Many claim to have unfailing love, but who can find a truly faithful person? ⁷ The righteous lead blameless lives; blessed are their children after them. ⁸ A king who sits on the throne of judgment scatters away all evil with his eyes. ⁹ Who can say, "I have kept my heart pure; I am clean and without sin"? ¹⁰ Differing weights and differing measures — the LORD detests them both.

¹¹ Even a child is known by their actions, by whether their conduct is pure and upright. ¹² Ears that hear and eyes that see — the LORD has made them both. ¹³ Do not love sleep or you will grow poor; stay awake and you will have food to spare. ¹⁴ "It's worthless, it's worthless!" says the buyer, but then goes off and boasts about the purchase. ¹⁵ Gold there is, and rubies in abundance, but lips that speak knowledge are a rare jewel.

¹⁶ Take the garment of one who puts up security for a stranger; hold it in pledge if it is done for an outsider. ¹⁷ Food gained by fraud tastes sweet, but one ends up with a mouth full of gravel. ¹⁸ Plans are established by seeking advice; so wage war with good guidance. ¹⁹ A gossip betrays a confidence; so avoid anyone who talks too much. ²⁰ Whoever curses their father or mother will have their lamp snuffed out in pitch darkness.

²¹ An inheritance claimed too soon in the beginning will not be blessed in the end. ²² Do not say, "I'll pay you back for this wrong!" Wait for the LORD, and he will avenge you. ²³ The LORD detests differing weights, and dishonest scales do not please him. ²⁴ A person's steps are directed by the LORD — so how can anyone understand their own way? ²⁵ It is a trap to dedicate something rashly and only later to consider your vows.

²⁶ A wise king sifts out the wicked; he drives the threshing wheel over them. ²⁷ The human spirit is the lamp of the LORD, searching out the inmost being. ²⁸ Love and faithfulness keep a king safe; through love his throne is made secure. ²⁹ The glory of young men is their strength, and the splendor of the old is their gray hair. ³⁰ Blows and wounds scrub away evil, and beatings purge the inmost being.

¹ In the LORD's hand the king's heart is a stream of water that he channels toward all who please him. ² A person may think their own ways are right, but the LORD weighs the heart. ³ To do what is right and just is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice. ⁴ Haughty eyes and a proud heart — the lamp of the wicked — are sin! ⁵ The plans of the diligent lead to profit as surely as haste leads to poverty.

⁶ A fortune made by a lying tongue is a fleeting vapor and a deadly snare. ⁷ The violence of the wicked will drag them away, for they refuse to do what is just. ⁸ The way of the guilty is devious, but the conduct of the innocent is upright. ⁹ Better to live on a corner of the roof than share a house with a quarrelsome wife. ¹⁰ The wicked crave evil; their neighbors get no mercy from them.

¹¹ When a mocker is punished, the simple gain wisdom; by paying attention to the wise they get knowledge. ¹² The Righteous One takes note of the house of the wicked and brings the wicked to ruin. ¹³ Whoever shuts their ears to the cry of the poor will also cry out and not be answered. ¹⁴ A gift given in secret soothes anger, and a bribe concealed in the cloak pacifies great wrath. ¹⁵ When justice is done, it brings joy to the righteous but terror to evildoers.

¹⁶ Whoever strays from the path of prudence comes to rest in the company of the dead. ¹⁷ Whoever loves pleasure will become poor; whoever loves wine and olive oil will never be rich. ¹⁸ The wicked become a ransom for the righteous, and the unfaithful for the upright. ¹⁹ Better to live in a desert than with a quarrelsome and nagging wife. ²⁰ The wise store up choice food and olive oil, but fools gulp theirs down.

²¹ Whoever pursues righteousness and love finds life, prosperity, and honor. ²² One who is wise can go up against the city of the mighty and pull down the stronghold in which they trust. ²³ Those who guard their mouths and tongues keep themselves from trouble. ²⁴ "Proud," "Conceited," "Mocker" — these are the names of those who act with haughty arrogance. ²⁵ The craving of a sluggard will be their death, because their hands refuse to work.

²⁶ All day long they crave for more, but the righteous give without holding back. ²⁷ The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable — how much more so when brought with evil intent! ²⁸ A false witness will perish, but the words of an attentive witness will endure. ²⁹ The wicked put on a bold face, but the upright direct their own steps. ³⁰ There is no wisdom, no insight, no plan that can succeed against the LORD.
